**Finding: Compliant** — no redline needed.

The agreement imposes no exclusivity on Bluefly:

- **§ 14.16 (Freedom of Action)** — mutual and favorable: "Each party is free to enter into similar agreements with others." This expressly protects our freedom to buy hosting from other suppliers. The planner's asymmetry concern doesn't apply, since the clause runs to both parties rather than reserving freedom of action to IBM alone.
- **§ 14.11 (No Resale)** — restricts only reselling the Services; a scope-of-use limit, not a requirements or sole-supplier covenant.
- **§ 13.1** — actually reinforces our optionality by allowing termination without termination charges if we disagree with IBM's changes.
- Remaining "exclusive" hits are unrelated: charges exclusive of taxes (§ 4.3), exclusive warranties disclaimer (§ 5.2), and nonexclusive license grants in our favor (§ 5.4, § 12.1).

A targeted sweep for sole-source/requirements-style phrasing ("sole supplier," "all of its requirements," "shall not procure," "preferred provider," "minimum volume," etc.) returned nothing, so the preferred playbook position is satisfied without amendment.
